pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — SEV2: Smart routing policy evaluation panic detected for routing-engine (service: router-prod). Significant fallback churn between regions; automatic fallbacks to model-variant 'small-quant' observed. Paging oncall: maya (oncall). Link: https://internal.pagerduty/INC-2204078901

maya (oncall): on it. seeing increased 5xx rate from router-prod in grafana. creating incident channel here.

rachit: stacktrace from router logs (tail):
```
panic: runtime error: index out of range
at policy_engine/eval.go:184 chooseVariant()
at router/handler.go:327 handleRequest()
```
seems to happen during the rule that maps customer metadata -> model_variant.

olivia: grabbing the rule definition now. looks like the rule uses an inline expression that indexes into metadata without a null check: `meta.variants[0]` — if `meta.variants` is missing it panics.

sam (incident lead): immediate mitigation we discussed: 1) disable the smart routing policy (turn off policy id 7) 2) pin default model variant for affected regions to `redwood-small-v1` 3) throttle new canaries. Who can flip the policy?

olivia: I can flip. making API call: `PATCH /admin/policies/7 {"enabled": false}` 

olivia: done — policy 7 set enabled=false (response 200). router config applied. switching fallback routing to static region mapping: `router.set_region_default("us-west-2","redwood-small-v1")`

alex: confirming traffic metrics — within 30s 5xx% dropped from 9.8% -> 1.2% across us-west. latency p95 back to baseline.

platform-sre: thanks. can we also add a temporary guard in policy engine to catch missing arrays to avoid panic on eval? put a defensive check in eval runtime.

rachit: yes, quick patch candidate: replace direct index with safe accessor `len(meta.variants)>0 ? meta.variants[0] : null`. pushing a hotfix to staging now.

sam (incident lead): customer impact?

customer-success: preliminary list: acme-corp (critical), learnco (enterprise), a small subset of free-tier requests. We're notifying acme-corp engineering and offering a status update.

maya (oncall): note for post-incident: policy tests missed this because test fixtures always included `variants` array. need to add negative tests.

rachit: patch landed to runtime in staging: `commit b9f4e2` adding safe indexing + unit tests. starting rollout to canary router nodes (10%).

olivia: re-enabled policy temporarily in read-only mode? we kept it disabled. do we want gradual re-enable after canary?

sam (incident lead): keep disabled until patch reaches 100% and we validate. postmortem action: rework policy authoring docs to emphasize nil-safe expressions and linting.

alex: monitoring — canary nodes on patched runtime show no eval panics after 2k requests/min with synthetic payloads.

platform-sre: production rollout plan: 1) patch runtime to 50% 2) monitor errors/latency 30m 3) if stable, roll to 100% 4) re-enable policy and watch for eval errors 30m.

customer-success: sent brief to acme-corp: "We observed elevated errors due to routing policy evaluation; we applied a temporary mitigation and are working on a permanent fix. Will follow up with timeline."

maya (oncall): upgrading incident severity -> SEV3 now (customer impact contained, core functionality restored).

rachit: runtime patch rolled to 100% at 2204079205. verification: no panics in logs since.

olivia: re-enabling policy 7 in disabled mode is still off. preparing to re-enable after additional validation.

sam (incident lead): at this point: mitigation successful, customers notified, patch deployed. owners:
- postmortem writeup: sam
- policy authoring lint + CI guard: maya + rachit
- customer follow-up and timeline: customer-success

platform-sre: creating a follow-up alert in grafana for any policy_engine panic > 0 to page oncall immediately.

maya (oncall): marking incident resolved in PD, will close once postmortem is posted.

customer-success: acme-corp replied, appreciates the quick mitigation, requested ETA for permanent guard. we'll coordinate.

sam (incident lead): resolution summary: root cause — policy expression performed an unsafe array index when metadata was missing which caused a runtime panic in the policy evaluator. impact — routing fallbacks and elevated 5xx for ~7 minutes while policy evaluation crashed on certain requests and triggered fallback behavior. mitigation — disabled policy, pinned default model variant, deployed safe-index runtime patch, rolled forward. follow-ups assigned.

rachit: temporary fix (safe index) also added unit and integration tests. will open a PR for stricter linter rules on expressions to block unsafe indexing in authored policies.

olivia: adding runbook note: always validate metadata shape before indexing, and add a CI check that runs policy expressions against empty/null fixtures.

sam (incident lead): closing: will publish postmortem doc within 48h. great work, team. :party_parrot:
